scope: Causal transport and controlled-input identifiability when the target interface supplies drift b and covariance rate A at every fully observed state and action.

claims.claim: There exist two finite-state controlled CTMCs with identical b(x,u) and A(x,u) at every observable state and action but different action-conditioned transition kernels and third jump moments.
claims.evidence: Five-state witness in CYCLE3_NOTE.md; moment identities checked by verify_witness.py.

claims.claim: The witness can have opposite target randomized effects on a bounded fate endpoint while all source response laws and all passive target path laws coincide across the invariant and reversal worlds.
claims.evidence: Analytic monotonicity of F_tau(theta) and exact controlled generator construction; finite numerical illustration is not the proof.

claims.claim: Equality of pointwise controlled drift/covariance fields alone is insufficient to transport arbitrary endpoint or full output-distribution effects.
claims.evidence: C3-01 and C3-02; conclusion is restricted to the declared CTMC class/interface.

claims.claim: Under strong controlled-HMM assumptions, signal-conditioned transition/emission parameters are identifiable from signal/output laws up to latent state bijections.
claims.evidence: David et al. (2024), Theorem 1; not automatically causal and not a source-to-target invariance theorem.

claims.claim: A target randomized endpoint panel with source and held-out context controls can distinguish this witness with nonasymptotic bounded-outcome intervals, while inconclusive cases remain possible.
claims.evidence: Hoeffding and union-bound design stated in CYCLE3_NOTE.md; costs and multi-endpoint extension linked to cycle 2.

claims.claim: This cycle establishes a novel universal cell-model perturbation transport theorem.
claims.evidence: Classical transportability, controlled-HMM identification, and reaction-network SDE identifiability precede the construction; no biological data or priority audit was performed.

unresolved: Biological state definitions, action, target engagement, donor-level variance, practical equivalence margins, and a target endpoint were not supplied.
Unknown hidden emissions need direct calibration or strong rank/anchor assumptions before latent state semantics can be transported.
Finite evidence in S/T/H supports only those named cell contexts, intervention versions, endpoints, and culture conditions; tissue/species/organism transfer remains unknown.
